Section D: Media

text: Different measurements of crime show the patterns of who commits crime and the types of crime
committed. Sociologists look at the data to try and determine why some people commit crime, for
example why age is a relevant factor. In some communities criminals experience ostracism. The
variety of crimes committed can make enforcement of the law and deterring criminals difficult.

text: Many sociologists believe that audiences are affected by what they consume in the media. This
can be media content, the language used and the representations shown. For example,
representations of some age groups can often lead to labelling in society. Many sociologists agree
the media is a powerful agent of socialisation and some censorship of the media may be necessary.
